## Link raw acquisitions to analytical records

`measure_record()` stores the relationships among samples, injections,
channels, sources, and one-dimensional curves. `measure_acquisition()` adds
stream declarations, per-scan spectra, and two-dimensional arrays. Each scan
keeps its own m/z coordinates and point order; scans need not share a grid.

This example starts with a small synthetic CSV written for the vignette. It is
not an instrument recording or a vendor export. The input contains point rows
and explicit scan-event rows for an acquired-empty scan and an unavailable
scan. Those states are not inferred from gaps in a sequence number.

```{r build-synthetic-source, include = FALSE}
guide_temp_dir <- tempfile("measure-acquisition-guide-")
dir.create(guide_temp_dir)
source_file <- file.path(guide_temp_dir, "synthetic-export.csv")

source_columns <- c(
  "record_type", "stream_key", "vendor_scan_key", "native_scan_ref",
  "sequence_no", "state", "rt_seconds", "ion_mode", "ms_stage",
  "representation", "mz_observed", "signal_observed", "saturation_flag",
  "array_key", "array_rt_seconds", "wavelength_nm", "array_signal",
  "array_sat_flag"
)

source_row <- function(...) {
  values <- as.list(rep(NA_character_, length(source_columns)))
  names(values) <- source_columns
  supplied <- list(...)
  values[names(supplied)] <- supplied
  as.data.frame(values, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

scan_row <- function(
  scan_id,
  source_scan_id,
  stream_id = "ms-centroid",
  scan_index,
  status = "acquired",
  retention_time,
  polarity = "positive",
  ms_level = 1L,
  spectrum_type = "centroid",
  mz = NA_character_,
  intensity = NA_character_,
  saturated = NA_character_,
  record_type = "scan-point"
) {
  source_row(
    record_type = record_type,
    stream_key = stream_id,
    vendor_scan_key = scan_id,
    native_scan_ref = source_scan_id,
    sequence_no = as.character(scan_index),
    state = status,
    rt_seconds = as.character(retention_time),
    ion_mode = polarity,
    ms_stage = as.character(ms_level),
    representation = spectrum_type,
    mz_observed = mz,
    signal_observed = intensity,
    saturation_flag = saturated
  )
}

array_row <- function(time, wavelength, value, saturated) {
  source_row(
    record_type = "array-point",
    stream_key = "array-2d",
    array_key = "array-01",
    array_rt_seconds = as.character(time),
    wavelength_nm = as.character(wavelength),
    array_signal = value,
    array_sat_flag = saturated
  )
}

synthetic_source <- do.call(
  rbind,
  list(
    scan_row("scan-p01", "fileScan=21", scan_index = 1L, retention_time = 0.25, mz = "100", intensity = "12.5", saturated = "0"),
    scan_row("scan-p01", "fileScan=21", scan_index = 1L, retention_time = 0.25, mz = "100", intensity = "2.5", saturated = "0"),
    scan_row("scan-n01", "fileScan=22", scan_index = 2L, retention_time = 0.4, polarity = "negative", mz = "100.2", intensity = "8.4", saturated = "0"),
    scan_row("scan-p02", "fileScan=23", scan_index = 3L, retention_time = 0.55, ms_level = 2L, mz = "50", intensity = "7", saturated = "0"),
    scan_row("scan-empty", "fileScan=25", scan_index = 5L, retention_time = 0.8, record_type = "scan-event"),
    scan_row("scan-unknown-mask", "fileScan=26", scan_index = 6L, retention_time = 1.0, mz = "100.5", intensity = "2.25"),
    scan_row("scan-missing-intensity", "fileScan=27", scan_index = 7L, retention_time = 1.3, mz = "100.75", intensity = NA_character_),
    scan_row("scan-outside-window", "fileScan=28", scan_index = 8L, retention_time = 1.6, mz = "300", intensity = "4", saturated = "0"),
    scan_row("scan-saturated", "fileScan=29", scan_index = 9L, retention_time = 1.9, mz = "100.2", intensity = "80", saturated = "1"),
    scan_row("scan-missing", "expected-event-12", scan_index = 12L, status = "missing", retention_time = 2.2, spectrum_type = NA_character_, record_type = "scan-event"),
    scan_row("scan-profile", "profileScan=1", stream_id = "ms-profile", scan_index = 1L, retention_time = 0.25, spectrum_type = "profile", mz = "99.7", intensity = "3.1"),
    array_row(0, 210, "0.15", "0"),
    array_row(0, 280, "0.27", "0"),
    array_row(0.75, 280, "0.43", NA_character_),
    array_row(1.5, 235, NA_character_, "0"),
    array_row(3, 320, "0.69", "1")
  )
)
rownames(synthetic_source) <- NULL
```

The column map below is the caller's import decision. Blank value cells become
ordinary missing values; blank saturation cells remain an unknown mask. The
row reference is the one-based ordinal in the parsed data frame, after its
header, rather than a physical text line number.

```{r create-and-parse-source}
source_fields <- c(
  record_kind = "record_type",
  stream_id = "stream_key",
  scan_id = "vendor_scan_key",
  source_scan_id = "native_scan_ref",
  scan_index = "sequence_no",
  scan_status = "state",
  retention_time = "rt_seconds",
  polarity = "ion_mode",
  ms_level = "ms_stage",
  spectrum_type = "representation",
  mz = "mz_observed",
  intensity = "signal_observed",
  saturated = "saturation_flag",
  array_id = "array_key",
  array_time = "array_rt_seconds",
  wavelength = "wavelength_nm",
  array_value = "array_signal",
  array_saturated = "array_sat_flag"
)

utils::write.csv(
  synthetic_source,
  file = source_file,
  row.names = FALSE,
  na = ""
)
parsed_source <- utils::read.csv(
  source_file,
  colClasses = "character",
  na.strings = "",
  check.names = FALSE,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
parsed_record_ordinal <- seq_len(nrow(parsed_source))
source_bytes <- readBin(
  source_file,
  what = "raw",
  n = file.info(source_file)$size
)
source_sha256 <- digest::digest(
  source_bytes,
  algo = "sha256",
  serialize = FALSE
)

knitr::kable(data.frame(
  file = basename(source_file),
  parsed_records = nrow(parsed_source),
  sha256 = source_sha256
))
```

## Map parsed rows into raw scans and an array

The importer below groups scan-point rows by the caller-mapped scan key. Event
rows retain acquired-empty and missing scan declarations without inventing a
point. Each raw point keeps its parsed-record ordinal in <code>.source_rows</code>;
m/z and intensity stay in the original within-scan order. The array stream
contains one sparse two-dimensional payload, with its own coordinates and axis
declarations.

<details>
<summary>Show the caller-side scan and array import mapping</summary>

```{r map-raw-acquisition, echo = TRUE, results = "hide"}
field <- function(name) parsed_source[[unname(source_fields[[name]])]]

parse_double <- function(x) {
  out <- rep(NA_real_, length(x))
  present <- !is.na(x) & nzchar(x)
  out[present] <- as.double(x[present])
  out
}

parse_mask <- function(x) {
  out <- rep(NA, length(x))
  present <- !is.na(x) & nzchar(x)
  if (!all(x[present] %in% c("0", "1"))) {
    stop("Saturation input must be coded as 0, 1, or blank.")
  }
  out[present] <- x[present] == "1"
  out
}

scan_id_input <- field("scan_id")
record_kind_input <- field("record_kind")
scan_input_rows <- which(
  !is.na(scan_id_input) &
    record_kind_input %in% c("scan-point", "scan-event")
)
scan_ids <- unique(scan_id_input[scan_input_rows])
scan_rows_by_id <- lapply(scan_ids, function(id) {
  scan_input_rows[scan_id_input[scan_input_rows] == id]
})
point_rows_by_scan <- lapply(scan_rows_by_id, function(rows) {
  rows[record_kind_input[rows] == "scan-point"]
})
scan_declarations <- lapply(seq_along(scan_rows_by_id), function(i) {
  rows <- scan_rows_by_id[[i]]
  declaration_fields <- c(
    "stream_id",
    "scan_index",
    "scan_status",
    "retention_time",
    "polarity",
    "ms_level",
    "spectrum_type",
    "source_scan_id"
  )
  for (name in declaration_fields) {
    if (length(unique(field(name)[rows])) != 1L) {
      stop("Conflicting scan declaration for ", scan_ids[[i]], ".")
    }
  }
  rows[[1L]]
})

scans <- tibble::tibble(
  scan_id = scan_ids,
  stream_id = vapply(
    scan_declarations,
    function(i) field("stream_id")[[i]],
    character(1)
  ),
  scan_index = as.integer(vapply(
    scan_declarations,
    function(i) field("scan_index")[[i]],
    character(1)
  )),
  scan_status = vapply(
    scan_declarations,
    function(i) field("scan_status")[[i]],
    character(1)
  ),
  retention_time = parse_double(vapply(
    scan_declarations,
    function(i) field("retention_time")[[i]],
    character(1)
  )),
  polarity = vapply(
    scan_declarations,
    function(i) field("polarity")[[i]],
    character(1)
  ),
  ms_level = as.integer(vapply(
    scan_declarations,
    function(i) field("ms_level")[[i]],
    character(1)
  )),
  spectrum_type = vapply(
    scan_declarations,
    function(i) field("spectrum_type")[[i]],
    character(1)
  ),
  source_scan_id = vapply(
    scan_declarations,
    function(i) field("source_scan_id")[[i]],
    character(1)
  ),
  .measures = lapply(point_rows_by_scan, function(rows) {
    new_measure_tbl(
      location = parse_double(field("mz")[rows]),
      value = parse_double(field("intensity")[rows])
    )
  }),
  .source_rows = lapply(point_rows_by_scan, function(rows) {
    as.integer(parsed_record_ordinal[rows])
  }),
  .saturated = lapply(point_rows_by_scan, function(rows) {
    parse_mask(field("saturated")[rows])
  })
)

array_point_rows <- which(
  record_kind_input == "array-point" & !is.na(field("array_id"))
)
array_ids <- unique(field("array_id")[array_point_rows])
array_rows_by_id <- lapply(array_ids, function(id) {
  array_point_rows[field("array_id")[array_point_rows] == id]
})

arrays <- tibble::tibble(
  array_id = array_ids,
  stream_id = vapply(
    array_rows_by_id,
    function(rows) field("stream_id")[[rows[[1L]]]],
    character(1)
  ),
  .measures = lapply(array_rows_by_id, function(rows) {
    new_measure_nd_tbl(
      location_1 = parse_double(field("array_time")[rows]),
      location_2 = parse_double(field("wavelength")[rows]),
      value = parse_double(field("array_value")[rows]),
      dim_names = c("retention_time", "wavelength"),
      dim_units = c("s", "nm")
    )
  }),
  .source_rows = lapply(array_rows_by_id, function(rows) {
    as.integer(parsed_record_ordinal[rows])
  }),
  .saturated = lapply(array_rows_by_id, function(rows) {
    parse_mask(field("array_saturated")[rows])
  })
)

record <- measure_record(
  samples = tibble::tibble(sample_id = "sample-A"),
  injections = tibble::tibble(
    injection_id = "injection-A",
    sample_id = "sample-A"
  ),
  channels = tibble::tibble(
    channel_id = c("ms-centroid", "ms-profile", "array-2d"),
    channel_name = c("MS centroid", "MS profile", "2D signal array")
  ),
  sources = tibble::tibble(
    source_id = "synthetic-csv",
    source_name = basename(source_file),
    source_sha256 = source_sha256
  )
)

streams <- tibble::tibble(
  stream_id = c("ms-centroid", "ms-profile", "array-2d"),
  injection_id = "injection-A",
  channel_id = c("ms-centroid", "ms-profile", "array-2d"),
  kind = c("ms", "ms", "nd"),
  source_id = "synthetic-csv",
  time_unit = c("s", "s", NA_character_),
  mz_unit = c("m/z", "m/z", NA_character_),
  value_name = c("ion abundance", "ion abundance", "signal"),
  value_unit = c("counts", "counts", "declared signal units")
)
```
</details>

The acquisition contains positive and negative scans at two MS levels, a
separate profile stream, and a 2D stream. The caller supplies IDs, units,
scan states, representations, saturation declarations, and array axis labels;
the constructor validates their relationships without inferring them.

```{r make-acquisition}
acquisition <- measure_acquisition(
  record = record,
  streams = streams,
  scans = scans,
  arrays = arrays
)
summary(acquisition)
```

The synthetic record has no scalar curves. Each trace value may summarize
multiple scan points, so the extracted trace remains linked to its raw
acquisition.

## Write and reload the raw acquisition first

The native profile is a fixed, flat twelve-table CSV bundle. This write/read
roundtrip happens before TIC or XIC calculation, so the calculations below use
the reloaded raw data.

```{r native-roundtrip}
native_path <- file.path(guide_temp_dir, "native-acquisition-v1")
write_measure_acquisition(acquisition, native_path, delim = ",")
raw_acquisition <- read_measure_acquisition(native_path)
summary(raw_acquisition)
```

```{r native-fidelity, include = FALSE}
stopifnot(identical(raw_acquisition, acquisition))
stopifnot(
  identical(raw_acquisition$scans$.source_rows, acquisition$scans$.source_rows),
  identical(raw_acquisition$scans$.saturated, acquisition$scans$.saturated),
  identical(raw_acquisition$arrays$.source_rows, acquisition$arrays$.source_rows),
  identical(raw_acquisition$arrays$.saturated, acquisition$arrays$.saturated)
)
```

Each scan retains its own point count and m/z coordinates. The bundle also
retains acquired-empty and missing scans, missing intensities, and the
three-valued saturation mask (`TRUE`, `FALSE`, or unknown) as separate states.

## Derive an explicit centroid TIC and XIC

The MS stream contains positive and negative scans and more than one MS level.
Selection is explicit: these traces request positive-ion MS1 scans in
<code>ms-centroid</code>. The XIC interval is closed in the stream's declared
m/z coordinate convention, stored as literal <code>m/z</code> in the schema's
<code>mz_unit</code> field. This is not a mass unit and no conversion is
performed. IUPAC defines mass-to-charge ratio as a quantity and discourages
assigning a mass unit to an m/z axis in its
[Gold Book entry](https://goldbook.iupac.org/terms/view/M03752.html) and
[recommendations](https://publications.iupac.org/pac/pdf/asap/pdf/PAC-REC-06-04-06.pdf).
Duplicate m/z points are kept as separate contributors.

```{r extract-traces}
tic <- measure_ms_trace(
  raw_acquisition,
  stream_id = "ms-centroid",
  polarity = "positive",
  ms_level = 1L
)

xic <- measure_ms_trace(
  raw_acquisition,
  stream_id = "ms-centroid",
  polarity = "positive",
  ms_level = 1L,
  mz_range = c(100, 101)
)
```

```{r trace-fidelity, include = FALSE}
stopifnot(
  identical(xic$scan_index, c(1L, 5L, 6L, 7L, 8L, 9L, 12L)),
  identical(xic$value[c(1L, 2L, 3L, 5L)], c(15, 0, 2.25, 0)),
  identical(xic$status, c(
    "calculated",
    "empty_scan",
    "calculated",
    "missing_intensity",
    "empty_window",
    "saturated",
    "missing_scan"
  )),
  identical(
    xic$.point_indices,
    list(1:2, integer(), 1L, 1L, integer(), 1L, integer())
  ),
  identical(
    xic$saturation_unknown,
    c(FALSE, FALSE, TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE)
  ),
  identical(tic$scan_index, xic$scan_index)
)
```

A finite sum with an unknown saturation mask is still marked
<code>saturation_unknown</code>; <code>calculated</code> describes arithmetic
and does not qualify a measurement method. A known saturated point produces an
unknown trace value, while an ordinary missing intensity produces a different
status.

```{r xic-results}
format_indices <- function(x) {
  vapply(x, function(index) paste(index, collapse = ", "), character(1))
}

xic_table <- tibble::tibble(
  scan_id = xic$scan_id,
  scan_index = xic$scan_index,
  retention_time_s = xic$retention_time,
  value = xic$value,
  status = xic$status,
  point_indices = format_indices(xic$.point_indices),
  saturation_unknown = xic$saturation_unknown
)
knitr::kable(xic_table, digits = 3)
```

This plot shows numeric results for the selected centroid XIC. The
acquired-empty scan and the empty m/z window both yield zero, with distinct
statuses. Missing-intensity, saturated, and missing-scan results have no
numeric value and are omitted here.

```{r xic-value-plot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5, fig.cap = "Numeric XIC results for the declared positive-ion, MS1 centroid selection. The acquired-empty scan and the scan with no point in the m/z window both return zero, with distinct statuses.", fig.alt = "Point chart of XIC intensity in counts against retention time in seconds. Scan 1 has a 15-count sum at 0.25 s from two m/z 100 contributors. Scan 5 is acquired-empty and has value zero at 0.8 s. Scan 6 has a 2.25-count result at 1.0 s with an unknown saturation mask. Scan 8 has value zero at 1.6 s because no point falls in the selected m/z interval. The acquired-empty and empty-window zeros have different shapes. Missing-intensity, saturated, and missing-scan results have no numeric value and are not plotted."}
xic_value_plot_data <- xic_table |>
  dplyr::filter(is.finite(value)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    status = factor(
      status,
      levels = c("calculated", "empty_scan", "empty_window")
    ),
    scan_label = paste0("scan ", scan_index)
  )

ggplot2::ggplot(
  xic_value_plot_data,
  ggplot2::aes(
    x = retention_time_s,
    y = value,
    colour = status,
    shape = status
  )
) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(size = 3) +
  ggplot2::geom_text(
    ggplot2::aes(label = scan_label),
    nudge_y = 0.55,
    size = 3,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(
    name = "Trace status",
    values = c(
      calculated = "#176B87",
      empty_scan = "#69757A",
      empty_window = "#3A7864"
    ),
    labels = c(
      calculated = "Calculated",
      empty_scan = "Acquired empty",
      empty_window = "Empty m/z window"
    )
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_shape_manual(
    name = "Trace status",
    values = c(calculated = 16, empty_scan = 15, empty_window = 17),
    labels = c(
      calculated = "Calculated",
      empty_scan = "Acquired empty",
      empty_window = "Empty m/z window"
    )
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = xic_value_plot_data$retention_time_s,
    expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.2))
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
    expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.15))
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "Retention time (s)",
    y = "XIC ion abundance (counts)"
  ) +
  guide_plot_theme
```

The status column distinguishes an acquired-empty scan from a missing scan,
a missing intensity, a saturated point, and a scan with no point in the XIC
window. Both an acquired-empty scan and an empty m/z window produce a numeric
zero here, with different statuses; missing-intensity, saturated, and
missing-scan results have no numeric trace value.

```{r xic-status-plot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5, fig.cap = "XIC status by retention time for the declared positive-ion, MS1 centroid selection. Acquired-empty scans and empty m/z windows both return zero, while missing-intensity, saturated, and missing-scan states remain separate.", fig.alt = "Categorical scatter chart of XIC result status. Retention time in seconds is on the x-axis and trace status is on the y-axis. Scan 1 is calculated at 0.25 s, scan 5 is acquired-empty with value zero at 0.8 s, scan 6 is calculated at 1.0 s, scan 7 has missing intensity at 1.3 s, scan 8 has an empty m/z window with value zero at 1.6 s, scan 9 is saturated at 1.9 s, and scan 12 is a missing scan at 2.2 s. The two zero-valued states retain different categories; missing-intensity, saturated, and missing-scan results have no numeric value."}
xic_status_levels <- c(
  "calculated",
  "empty_scan",
  "missing_intensity",
  "empty_window",
  "saturated",
  "missing_scan"
)
xic_status_plot_data <- xic_table |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    status = factor(status, levels = xic_status_levels),
    scan_label = paste0("scan ", scan_index)
  )

ggplot2::ggplot(
  xic_status_plot_data,
  ggplot2::aes(x = retention_time_s, y = status, colour = status)
) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(size = 3) +
  ggplot2::geom_text(
    ggplot2::aes(label = scan_label),
    nudge_x = 0.06,
    hjust = 0,
    size = 3,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(
      calculated = "#176B87",
      empty_scan = "#69757A",
      missing_intensity = "#C05A2B",
      empty_window = "#3A7864",
      saturated = "#A52A2A",
      missing_scan = "#7356A2"
    ),
    guide = "none"
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_discrete(
    labels = c(
      calculated = "Calculated",
      empty_scan = "Acquired empty",
      missing_intensity = "Missing intensity",
      empty_window = "Empty m/z window",
      saturated = "Saturated",
      missing_scan = "Missing scan"
    )
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(
    expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0.03, 0.3))
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "Retention time (s)",
    y = "XIC result status"
  ) +
  guide_plot_theme
```

The corresponding TIC sums all points in the same selected scans. Both traces
are derived from the raw spectra, not source-reported chromatograms.

```{r tic-results}
knitr::kable(tibble::tibble(
  scan_index = tic$scan_index,
  retention_time_s = tic$retention_time,
  value = tic$value,
  status = tic$status
), digits = 3)
```

The trace processing attribute records the selectors, units, source digest,
aggregation, missing-intensity policy, saturation policy, and lack of
synchronization.

```{r processing-declaration}
trace_processing <- attr(xic, "processing")
trace_processing
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  operation = trace_processing$operation,
  stream = trace_processing$stream_id,
  source_sha256 = trace_processing$source_sha256,
  mz_range = paste(trace_processing$mz_range, collapse = " to "),
  mz_convention = trace_processing$mz_unit,
  time_unit = trace_processing$time_unit,
  aggregation = trace_processing$aggregation,
  missing_intensity = trace_processing$missing_intensity,
  saturation = trace_processing$saturation,
  synchronization = trace_processing$synchronization
))
```

## Follow trace points back to parsed input rows

The <code>.point_indices</code> list addresses positions within one retained
scan spectrum. For each selected scan, index the corresponding
<code>.source_rows</code> vector at those positions. The resulting parsed CSV
record ordinals point back to source rows. They do not collapse extraction
into a one-source-row scalar observation.

<details>
<summary>Show how trace point indices map to input rows</summary>

```{r linked-points, echo = TRUE, results = "hide"}
link_parts <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(xic)), function(i) {
  point_index <- xic$.point_indices[[i]]
  if (length(point_index) == 0L) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  scan_row <- match(xic$scan_id[[i]], raw_acquisition$scans$scan_id)
  source_row <- raw_acquisition$scans$.source_rows[[scan_row]][point_index]
  saturation <- raw_acquisition$scans$.saturated[[scan_row]][point_index]

  data.frame(
    scan_id = xic$scan_id[[i]],
    scan_index = xic$scan_index[[i]],
    point_index = point_index,
    parsed_csv_record = source_row,
    mz = raw_acquisition$scans$.measures[[scan_row]]$location[point_index],
    intensity = raw_acquisition$scans$.measures[[scan_row]]$value[point_index],
    saturated = saturation
  )
})
trace_point_links <- do.call(
  rbind,
  link_parts[!vapply(link_parts, is.null, logical(1))]
)
rownames(trace_point_links) <- NULL
```
</details>

```{r linked-points-fidelity, include = FALSE}
stopifnot(
  identical(trace_point_links$parsed_csv_record, c(1L, 2L, 6L, 7L, 9L))
)
```

The table shows each selected contributor's position in its scan and parsed
CSV record ordinal. It includes the two distinct m/z 100 points in scan 1, a
point with missing intensity, and a point declared saturated.

```{r linked-points-output}
knitr::kable(trace_point_links, digits = 3)
```

This plot maps each XIC contributor from its parsed CSV record to its scan.
Point labels give the within-scan point index; shape marks whether an intensity
is present, and color shows the point's saturation mask. The two m/z 100
contributors in scan 1 remain separate points.

```{r trace-lineage-plot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5, fig.cap = "Parsed CSV records contributing to the selected XIC, mapped to scan indices. Labels give within-scan point indices; shape indicates whether an intensity is present, and color indicates the declared saturation mask.", fig.alt = "Lineage scatter chart with parsed CSV data-record ordinal on the x-axis and scan index on the y-axis. Rows 1 and 2 map to scan 1 as separate numeric points at the same m/z coordinate; row 6 maps to scan 6 with numeric intensity and an unknown saturation mask. Row 7 maps to scan 7 with missing intensity and an unknown mask. Row 9 maps to scan 9 with numeric intensity marked saturated. Point labels give within-scan indices."}
trace_point_plot_data <- trace_point_links |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    intensity_state = ifelse(
      is.na(intensity),
      "Missing intensity",
      "Numeric intensity"
    ),
    saturation_state = dplyr::case_when(
      is.na(saturated) ~ "Saturation unknown",
      saturated ~ "Declared saturated",
      TRUE ~ "Declared not saturated"
    ),
    point_label = paste0("p", point_index)
  )

ggplot2::ggplot(
  trace_point_plot_data,
  ggplot2::aes(
    x = parsed_csv_record,
    y = scan_index,
    colour = saturation_state,
    shape = intensity_state
  )
) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(size = 3) +
  ggplot2::geom_text(
    ggplot2::aes(label = point_label),
    nudge_y = 0.28,
    size = 3,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(
    name = "Saturation mask",
    values = c(
      "Declared not saturated" = "#176B87",
      "Saturation unknown" = "#C05A2B",
      "Declared saturated" = "#A52A2A"
    ),
    labels = c(
      "Declared not saturated" = "Not saturated",
      "Saturation unknown" = "Unknown",
      "Declared saturated" = "Saturated"
    )
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_shape_manual(
    name = "Intensity",
    values = c(
      "Numeric intensity" = 16,
      "Missing intensity" = 15
    ),
    labels = c(
      "Numeric intensity" = "Numeric",
      "Missing intensity" = "Missing"
    )
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = sort(unique(trace_point_plot_data$parsed_csv_record)),
    minor_breaks = NULL
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = sort(unique(trace_point_plot_data$scan_index)),
    minor_breaks = NULL
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "Parsed CSV data-record ordinal",
    y = "Scan index (within stream)"
  ) +
  ggplot2::guides(
    colour = ggplot2::guide_legend(nrow = 1),
    shape = ggplot2::guide_legend(nrow = 1)
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    legend.box = "vertical",
    legend.justification = "left"
  ) +
  guide_plot_theme
```

## Preserve profile data without applying centroid arithmetic

The profile stream's coordinates and intensities remain in the acquisition.
The centroid trace operation rejects it rather than summing profile samples as
though they were discrete centroid peaks.

```{r profile-retained}
profile_row <- match("scan-profile", raw_acquisition$scans$scan_id)
profile_spectrum <- raw_acquisition$scans$.measures[[profile_row]]
profile_spectrum

profile_attempt <- tryCatch(
  measure_ms_trace(
    raw_acquisition,
    stream_id = "ms-profile",
    polarity = "positive",
    ms_level = 1L
  ),
  error = function(error) conditionMessage(error)
)
profile_attempt
```

```{r profile-policy, include = FALSE}
stopifnot(
  identical(raw_acquisition$scans$spectrum_type[[profile_row]], "profile"),
  is.character(profile_attempt),
  grepl("centroid", profile_attempt, fixed = TRUE)
)
```

## Keep the 2D array on its own grid

The array stream preserves its sparse, nonuniform coordinate pairs, missing
signal, and point-level mask. Its declared axes are retention time in seconds
and wavelength in nanometres. Two dimensions by themselves do not establish
that a payload is a physical DAD measurement. The array keeps its own sparse
coordinate grid; it is not regridded to scan order or an MS m/z axis.

```{r array-retained}
array_row <- match("array-01", raw_acquisition$arrays$array_id)
array_payload <- raw_acquisition$arrays$.measures[[array_row]]
array_table <- tibble::tibble(
  parsed_csv_record = raw_acquisition$arrays$.source_rows[[array_row]],
  retention_time_s = array_payload$location_1,
  wavelength_nm = array_payload$location_2,
  signal = array_payload$value,
  saturated = raw_acquisition$arrays$.saturated[[array_row]]
)
knitr::kable(array_table, digits = 3)
```

## Capabilities and limits

| Capability | This slice |
|:--|:--|
| Input in this guide | A synthetic CSV read by the caller with an explicit column map; there is no package CSV, vendor, mzML, or mzXML acquisition reader. |
| Native acquisition storage | The write/read functions round-trip the fixed measure-acquisition version 1 profile. |
| Python validation | An independent project decoder can check the native tables and hand-calculated traces; this is a qualification path, not a package Python importer. |
| External readers | No named external-reader interoperability is implemented here. |

This API retains scan metadata, ragged raw spectra, explicit missingness and
saturation states, arrays, and derivation links. It does not infer ion or
precursor identities, align features or scans, integrate profile data, match
libraries, synchronize streams, or qualify an instrument or analytical
method. The CSV and native bundle in this example are temporary teaching
artifacts, removed after rendering.

The scan-per-spectrum model is consistent with distinctions in the
[PSI-MS controlled vocabulary](https://github.com/HUPO-PSI/psi-ms-CV/blob/master/psi-ms.obo)
and with the per-spectrum metadata and peak vectors in the
[Spectra package manual](https://bioconductor.org/packages/3.23/bioc/manuals/Spectra/man/Spectra.pdf).
Those are data-model precedents only; this vignette does not claim PSI
validation, Spectra interoperability, or an mzML reader.
